summary: David DiNardo lays out the two-part growth strategy he is running in real time for Taxifi: a personal brand that sells nothing and exists only to build trust through free organic content, and a product that converts that trust through Meta ads. After a year of daily posting on TikTok, Instagram and LinkedIn and launching the Laid Off to 8 Figures podcast, he explains how each platform serves a different audience, why he chases connection over virality, and why every successful guest on the show built a community before a product.
takeaways: Separate the two jobs: the personal brand builds trust with free content and never sells, while the business runs paid direct-to-consumer ads to convert that trust into customers.

David's posting speed went from about four hours for three TikToks to 30 minutes for three, so he now blocks 30 minutes a day for TikTok, three to five Instagram stories plus one reel or post, and business-only content for his 10,000-plus LinkedIn followers.

He measures connection rather than virality: a thousand views that earn 50 to 100 likes and DMs from people following the whole journey is the signal that trust is forming, and any video that tries to sell goes nowhere.
Since launching Meta ads on March 1, conversions to the Taxifi waitlist happen faster because prospects have already seen a year of trust-building content.
Every successful founder who has appeared on the podcast built the community first and the product second; expect to take a financial hit building organic reach before advertising pays off.

His prescription for any business owner: spend one to two hours a day on one post on one platform, and make it about you and the business, not just the business, even if talking about your personal life feels intimidating.
